Simulate networks from an MRQAP

Source: R/interpret_simulate.R
simulate_mrqap.Rd

simulate() draws outcome networks from an MRQAP, conditional on its covariates. It has three methods, which give the same networks for the same coefficients, the same network, and the same seed:

  • simulate(fit), for an infernetMrqapFit from estimate_mrqap();

  • simulate(coefs, .data = net), for a set of coefficients from declare_coefs();

  • simulate(spec, coefs = , .data = net), for a specification from specify_mrqap() and its coefficients.

test_gof() draws its simulations of an infernetMrqapFit with the same simulator.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapFit'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = getOption("snet_computation")$seed,
  .data = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapCoefs'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = getOption("snet_computation")$seed,
  .data,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mrqap_formula'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = getOption("snet_computation")$seed,
  .data,
  coefs,
  family = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An infernetMrqapFit from estimate_mrqap(), a set of coefficients from declare_coefs(), or a specification from specify_mrqap().

nsim

The number of networks to simulate.

seed

A seed for the random draws. By default, the seed set with set_control_computation(), if any. The random state of the session is put back after a draw with a seed.

.data

The network that the model builds its columns on. For a fit, the network that it was fitted on. It is optional for a fit: without it, the result is a list of stocnet networks, in which the cells outside the model are empty.

...

Not used.

coefs

For a specification, the coefficients: a set from declare_coefs(), or a named vector such as stats::coef(fit).

family, sigma

For a specification with a plain vector of coefficients, the family and, for a "gaussian" model, the standard deviation of the residuals, as in declare_coefs(). family = NULL, the default, takes the family of a set from declare_coefs(), or else reads it from the outcome in .data, as estimate_mrqap() does.

Value

A list of nsim networks, of the class of .data, or of class stocnet without it.

Details

Each simulation draws a tie in each dyad that the model used, from the model's predicted value there: a Bernoulli draw for "binomial", a Poisson draw for "poisson", and a normal draw with standard deviation sigma for "gaussian". The other cells of the outcome, such as an unobserved dyad or a fixed tie, keep their value in .data, or are empty without it. An undirected network is mirrored.

A fit draws from its coefficients where its family is "gaussian", "binomial", or "poisson" and it has no random or fixed effects. Otherwise it draws with stats::simulate() of the observed model, which it keeps with "model" in outputs. A set of coefficients and a specification draw only from a model without random or fixed effects. A list of networks, a panel, and a cognitive social structure cannot yet be simulated.

simulate() is conditional on the covariates of the network. {manynet}'s generate_*() functions are not.

Each simulation has its own random stream, so a seed gives the same networks whether they are drawn sequentially or in parallel. The ncores and strategy set with set_control_computation() choose the plan.

See also

declare_coefs() for a set of coefficients, and test_gof(), which compares the observed network with these simulations.

Other interpreting functions: play_diffusions(), predict_mrqap, sweep

Examples

fit <- estimate_mrqap(friends ~ social + tasks, ison_algebra, times = 5,
                      control = list(family = "poisson"))
nets <- simulate(fit, nsim = 2, seed = 1, .data = ison_algebra)
nets[[1]]
#> # A weighted, directed network of 16 nodes and 49 arcs
#> 
#> ── Ties 
#> # A tibble: 49 × 3
#>    from    to weight
#>   <int> <int>  <dbl>
#> 1     1     7      1
#> 2     1    10      2
#> 3     2     5      1
#> 4     2     6      1
#> 5     2     7      1
#> 6     2     8      2
#> # ℹ 43 more rows
#> 

# The same networks, from the coefficients of the fit
coefs <- declare_coefs(fit)
same <- simulate(coefs, nsim = 2, seed = 1, .data = ison_algebra)

# Or from a specification and coefficients that are stated
spec <- specify_mrqap(friends ~ social + tasks)
sims <- simulate(spec, nsim = 2, seed = 1, .data = ison_algebra,
                 coefs = c("(Intercept)" = -1, social = 0.5, tasks = 0),
                 family = "poisson")

# The family read from a 0/1 outcome
adolescents <- manynet::mutate_nodes(ison_adolescents, age = 11:18)
binary <- simulate(specify_mrqap(. ~ ego(age)), seed = 1, .data = adolescents,
                   coefs = c("(Intercept)" = -2, ego_age = 0.1))
